summary: Hybrid-embedding mix causing non-monotonic rerank scores and intermittent latency spikes on /v1/rerank
description:
Issue summary:
Customers using LuminaSearch have reported that rerank responses for the /v1/rerank endpoint show non-monotonic score order (results are not consistently descending by score) and occasional 200 responses that contain unexpected score inversions. In parallel, end-to-end latency to /v1/rerank has spiked from p95 ~120ms to p95 ~950ms for batches with >= 8 candidates.
Impact:
- Production impact for LuminaSearch search relevance; observed user-visible result reordering and slower page load.
- Affects both streaming and non-streaming rerank flows when hybrid embeddings (concatenation of sparse token features + dense vector) are used.
Environment:
- Prod us-east cluster serving dedicated tenant LuminaSearch. Rerank service behind API gateway, using per-tenant embedding encoder which can return either pure-dense or hybrid embeddings depending on dataset.
Steps to reproduce (observed by customer + reproducible via repro):
1) Create a rerank request with 1 query and 16 candidates. Ensure encoder returns hybrid embeddings (dense 768 concat sparse 128).
2) Call /v1/rerank with rerank_type=cosine and top_k=5.
3) Observe returned scores: sometimes candidate with lower cosine distance has higher returned score and appears above better-scoring candidate.
4) Repeat ~10-20 times; non-deterministic inversion occurs ~15-25% of runs in prod for these payloads.
5) Observe latency spikes on same requests correlated with CPU fallback traces and cache misses.
Logs / sample traces:
- API Gateway trace: request_id=req-8a7f, latency=1.2s, route=/v1/rerank
- Rerank service: trace_id=rr-3c4a, stage=score_compute, kernel_path=quant-fallback-cpu, kv_cache_hit=false
- Encoder logs: encoder_resp=(type=hybrid, dims=[896], format=concatenated, encoding_version=2026-02-28)
- Score diff snapshot: candidate A cosine=0.842, candidate B cosine=0.856, returned_score_A=0.89, returned_score_B=0.83
Observed anomalies / notes:
- Inversions only appear when encoder returns concatenated hybrid vectors. Pure-dense-only requests do not exhibit the inversion.
- When rerank service triggers quantized kernel fallback to CPU (on certain nodes under memory pressure), scores can flip.
- KV prefix cache behavior: some repeated queries have cache miss leading to recomputation on a different codepath, coincident with inversions.
- The encoder version header differs from the model catalog entry for this tenant (encoder reports 2026-02-28 vs catalog expects 2026-03-02).
Hypotheses:
1) Mixing sparse and dense components without consistent normalization leads to non-comparable cosine outputs when different compute paths apply different post-processing (e.g., legacy L2-normalization applied on dense-only path but skipped on hybrid path).
2) Quantization/CPU-fallback uses an alternate scoring implementation that treats concatenated vectors incorrectly (e.g., applies per-segment scaling twice).
3) Cache invalidation creates replay on nodes with mismatched encoder versions causing inconsistent normalization.
Affected customer impact: high. Customer reported production-facing regression and asked for immediate workaround while we investigate.
comments: 2026-03-13 15:12 - Sofia Patel: Customer LuminaSearch reported rerank result ordering changes plus latency. Provided example payloads and sample request_ids. Requested P1 escalation.
2026-03-13 15:40 - Daniel Kim: Acknowledged. Started repro locally using customer's payload. Observed non-deterministic score inversions. Raising to Serving-Infra. Linked to quant fallback traces.

2026-03-13 16:05 - Priya Rao (Serving Infra): On initial look, nodes that hit the quant-fallback path show a different postprocess flag. Adding hypothesis that normalization step is conditionally skipped for concat vectors in CPU path.

2026-03-13 17:10 - LuminaSearch (customer): Confirmed issue reproducible across EU and US traffic. They can force encoder to output dense-only as a temporary change but that reduces recall and is not acceptable long-term.

2026-03-14 09:23 - Daniel Kim: Deployed repro instrumented build to a staging pod (rr-staging-3). Captured detailed per-segment norms: dense_norm=0.999, sparse_norm=0.42 on CPU fallback; dense_norm=0.999, sparse_norm=0.98 on GPU path.

2026-03-14 13:02 - Priya Rao: Created draft PR to align normalization code paths between GPU and CPU kernels (github.com/redwood/serving/pull/2049). Still running perf tests; early results show inversion frequency drop to <2%.

2026-03-14 14:40 - Daniel Kim: Notified customer of mitigation steps and plan for a hotfix. Customer requested timeline for production patch and asked for a config toggle to force dense-only encoding as short-term mitigation.
investigation_notes: Repro: local repro with customer's encoder payload produced similar non-monotonic outputs ~18% of runs.
Trace analysis: quant-fallback CPU path applies per-segment scale factor 'sparse_scale' that is double-applied in current CPU scoring microcode (confirmed by reading scoring.cc:line~412).
Caching: prefix/KV cache miss correlated with recompute on node with older scoring binary (v1.11) leading to inconsistent behavior when autoscaler moves traffic.
Encoder-version drift: tenant-bound encoder images on some dedicated nodes are 1 commit behind catalog, likely due to staggered deploys for dedicated clusters.
next_steps: Ship hotfix aligning CPU and GPU normalization code paths (PR 2049) and roll out to prod us-east in canary then full rollout.
Add a server-side feature flag to force encoder to emit dense-only vectors for affected tenants as temporary mitigation.
Invalidate and warm KV prefix cache for LuminaSearch after rollout to avoid mixed-codepath replays.
Schedule postmortem and add a regression test in CI covering hybrid embeddings across quant/fallback paths.
Notify customer of timeline: canary deploy in next 4 hours, full rollout within 24 hours pending telemetry.
resolution_notes: TBD - awaiting hotfix verification in canary. Will update when full rollout completes.
